diagnostic_evidence.quote: Remind that the left singular vectors of $R_1$ constitute an orthonormal basis of $\mathbb{R}^2$.

issues.failure_explanation: The singular-value decomposition of R_1 gives R_1 u = \sigma_1 c_1(u)\alpha^{(1)} + \mu_1 d_1(u)\beta^{(1)} as a vector in R^2. Under the usual identification of R^2 with C, this corresponds to \widehat{w}^{(1)}u = \sigma_1 c_1(u)\alpha^{(1)} + \mu_1 d_1(u)\beta^{(1)} (with \alpha^{(1)},\beta^{(1)} regarded as complex numbers). The displayed extra factor \sqrt{-1} multiplying \mu_1 d_1(u)\beta^{(1)} is incompatible with \alpha^{(1)} and \beta^{(1)} being an orthonormal real basis: it would generally introduce cross terms in |\widehat{w}^{(1)}u|^2, whereas the later displayed OSF formula contains only the diagonal terms (1\pm W_1)c_1^2 and (1\mp W_1)d_1^2.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Correct (w1u) to the standard SVD expression, e.g. \widehat{w}^{(1)}u=\sigma_1 c_1(u)\alpha^{(1)}+\mu_1 d_1(u)\beta^{(1)} after identifying R^2 with C, or equivalently adjust the notation for \beta^{(1)} so that the expression is consistent with R_1u.
issues.overall_effect: The theorem statement in euclidean0 contains a false displayed equation. This undermines the source's internal SVD-based derivation of the Euclidean oscillation formulas, although the main geometric claims about the ellipse and the subsequent bounds are not independently false.
issues.title: Erroneous SVD expression for \widehat{w}^{(1)}u in the Euclidean theorem
issues.why_classification: This is a local one-symbol correction inside an illustrative Euclidean theorem. It preserves the stated ellipse, the singular-value identities, the OSF/OT formulas, and all downstream bounds and conclusions.

issues.failure_explanation: Let v_1 be the first column of the displayed V, namely v_1=(1+\sqrt{-1},\,1+\sqrt{-1},\,1+0.9\sqrt{-1})^T. Direct multiplication by the displayed A gives (Av_1)_3 = 18.1(1+\sqrt{-1})-19(1+0.9\sqrt{-1}) = -0.9+\sqrt{-1}, whereas (i v_1)_3 = \sqrt{-1}(1+0.9\sqrt{-1}) = -0.9+0.9\sqrt{-1}. Hence Av_1 \neq i v_1, so the displayed A is not equal to V\,\mathrm{diag}(i,-i,-1)\,V^{-1} with the displayed V. The later numerical data (V_1, W_1, R_1, f_1) are consistent with the displayed A, not with the displayed V.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Keep the displayed A and replace V by a correct eigenvector matrix of that A (the one giving the stated R_1 and numerical values), or alternatively change A to the matrix actually equal to V\,\mathrm{diag}(i,-i,-1)\,V^{-1} and recompute all example quantities. The least loss-preserving repair is the former, since the subsequent numerical values match the displayed A.
issues.overall_effect: The spectral construction of the example in Subsection 7.6 is false as written. The example's numerical claims remain meaningful for the displayed A, but the stated relation between A and the displayed V is unreliable until one of the two matrices is corrected.
issues.title: Displayed V does not diagonalize the displayed A in the highly oscillating example
issues.why_classification: The defect is confined to an illustrative example. A routine eigenvector computation gives a source-supported local correction that preserves the example's advertised behavior and all numerical conclusions associated with the displayed A.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Thus, for the vector $p$-norm, $p\in\{1,2,\infty\}$, we have strong evidence that in the vast majority of cases of a rightmost real eigenvalue

issues.failure_explanation: The sentence explicitly discusses the vector p-norm for p in {1,2,\infty}. For a general p-norm, \widehat{y}_0=y_0/\|y_0\|_p, so 1/|\widehat{w}^{(1)}\widehat{y}_0| = \|w^{(1)}\|_* \|y_0\|_p / |w^{(1)}y_0|, where \|w^{(1)}\|_* is the dual norm associated with the chosen p-norm. Replacing \|y_0\|_p by \|y_0\|_2 is only valid for the Euclidean norm p=2. As written, the displayed equality is false for p=1 and p=\infty.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Change \left\Vert y_0 \right\Vert_2 to \left\Vert y_0 \right\Vert_p (with \left\Vert w^{(1)} \right\Vert interpreted as the corresponding dual norm), or restrict the displayed equality to the Euclidean norm p=2.
issues.overall_effect: The displayed formula (KandK+) is incorrect in the general p-norm context in which it is stated. The surrounding empirical claim about the order of magnitude of max_t K(t,y_0) and K_\infty(y_0) is not materially affected, but the explicit algebraic equality is unreliable for non-Euclidean p-norms.
issues.title: P-norm statement uses \|y_0\|_2 in the formula for K_\infty(y_0)
issues.why_classification: This is a one-line local norm-mismatch correction. The advertised p-norm scope and the qualitative conclusion about order of magnitude survive without any new proof architecture or loss of a substantive result.
